proved_claims.statement: For g(x)=E phi_T(x-M) with H=E T^{-1/2}<infinity, Var(g)<=sqrt(2/pi) H, with arbitrary dependence of M and T and no moment condition on M.

For E_N=union_{j=1}^N[4j,4j+1/N], f_N=1_{E_N}, and any Gaussian location-scale mixture density g with inverse-scale budget H, H>=N sqrt(2pi)(1-||g-f_N||_1). Therefore H<=sqrt(2pi) implies ||g-f_N||_1>=1-1/N.

For X_N=M_N+(2N)^{-1}G with M_N uniform on {4,8,...,4N}, the marginal density is <0.799 while E T^{-1/2}=2N. For three independent copies and A=I_3, the conditional Gaussian component certificate is (2 I_3/pi)N^2 whereas completed source Theorem A gives ||p_Q||inf<=6sqrt(pi) uniformly in N.

partner_used.use: Its exact finite-fragment law E_N was inserted into the BV budget theorem to obtain the quantitative inverse-scale approximation lower bound. Its rank-two receiver counterexample was not promoted to the QFORM target.

required_source_used.use: Applied to Q_N=sum_{i=1}^3 X_{N,i}^2, A=I_3, to obtain ||p_QN||inf<=6sqrt(pi) uniformly in N and translations.

other_source_used.use: Conditional Gaussian Fourier density bound and inverse-scale hypothesis; used to quantify the N^2 component-first loss.

corrections_respected: Partner rank-two receiver obstruction is not a QFORM counterexample.

first_unpaid_implication.statement: Before reciprocal component scale or curvature is paid, aggregate translation/fragment labels at whole-law level, or use a whole-law D'/D5/projected-crossing/hub/pair/ridge certificate. Uniform inverse-scale Gaussian-mixture approximation of arbitrary cap-one finite-fragment laws is quantitatively impossible.
